'''Igor Youriévitch Bogdanoff''' ({{IPA|fr|iɡɔʁ juʁi.evitʃ bɔɡdanɔf}}; 29 August 1949 – 3 January 2022) and '''Grégoire''' "'''Grichka'''" '''Youriévitch Bogdanoff''' ({{IPA|fr|ɡʁeɡwaʁ ɡʁiʃka|lang}}; 29 August 1949 – 28 December 2021), alternatively spelled '''Bogdanov''', were French television presenters,<ref>Luis Gonzalez-Mestres, ''L'Énigme Bogdanov'', Éditions Télémaque, Paris, 2015, 320 p., {{ISBN|978-2-7533-0266-2}}</ref> producers, and essayists who presented a variety of programmes in science fiction, popular science, and [[cosmology]]. The brothers – identical twins – were involved in a number of controversies, the most notable being the [[Bogdanov affair]]. It brought to light how they received [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degrees<ref name="overbye"/> based on largely nonsensical [[physics]] papers that were nonetheless peer-reviewed and published in reputable scientific journals.<ref name="overbye"/> In their later years, they were also the subject of numerous [[internet meme]]s, particularly in the [[cryptocurrency]] community.

== Early life and disputed claims about ancestry ==
[[File:Berta Kolowrat-Krakowská (1890–1982) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|The twins' maternal grandmother, Countess Bertha Kolowrat-Krakowská|150px]]

The identical twin brothers Igor and Grichka Bogdanoff were born to Maria "Maya" Dolores Franzyska Kolowrat-Krakowská (1926–1982), of Bohemian and Polish descent, and Yuri "Youri" Mikhaïlovitch Bogdanoff (1928–2012),<ref>{{cite web|title=Youra Bogdanoff, père des célèbres frères Igor et Grishka Bogdanoff est décédé cette semaine. D'origine russe, il était né le 28 janvier 1928 à Saint-Pétersbourg. Artiste-peintre, il s'était établi à Saint-Lary avec son épouse Maya, avant la naissance de leurs premiers enfants, Igor et Grichka. Les frères Bogdanoff ont quatre frères et sœurs plus jeunes : François, Laurence, Géraldine et Véronique. Un recueillement en sa mémoire aura lieu le mercredi 8 août, à 11 heures, au cimetière de Saint-Lary. La Dépêche du Midi présente ses condoléances à la famille (Youra Bogdanof)|trans-title= father of famous brothers Igor and Grishka Bogdanoff died this week. Of Russian origin, he was born on 28 January 1928 in Saint Petersburg. Artist-painter, he had settled in Saint-Lary with his wife Maya, before the birth of their first children, Igor and Grichka. The Bogdanoff brothers have four younger siblings: François, Laurence, Géraldine and Véronique. A meditation in his memory will take place on Wednesday 8 August, at 11 a.m., at the Saint-Lary cemetery. La Dépêche du Midi presents its condolences to the family|url= https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2012/08/05/1413498-le-pere-des-bogdanoff-est-decede.html|website=ladepeche.fr}}</ref> an itinerant Russian ''[[Russian diaspora|emigré]]'' farm worker and later painter; Igor was born 40 minutes before Grichka. The twins' parents divorced shortly after their birth, and they were mainly raised by their maternal grandmother Bertha [[Kolowrat-Krakowsky#The Kolowrat-Krakowsky Line|Kolowrat-Krakowská]] at her castle in [[Saint-Lary, Gers|Saint-Lary]]. Their mother was born from an extramarital affair between Bertha (at the time married to Count Hieronymus [[House of Colloredo-Mannsfeld|Colloredo-Mannsfeld]]<ref name="ghda">Genealogisches Handbuch des Adels, Fürstliche Häuser  XIX. "Colloredo-Mannsfeld". C.A. Starke Verlag, 2011, pp. 127–29. (in German); {{ISBN|978-3-7980-0849-6}}</ref><ref name="kolowrat">Brooks, Christopher A. [https://books.google.com/books?id=z9wMBQAAQBAJ&dq=Bogdanoff+Kolowrat&pg=PA379 Roland Hayes: ''The Legacy of an American Tenor'']. [[Indiana University Press]]. Bloomington. 2015. pp. 358, 361–62, 366–67, 379; {{ISBN|978-0-253-01536-5}}</ref>) and African-American tenor [[Roland Hayes]]; their affair caused a major scandal and cost Bertha her title, access to her four elder children, palatial homes in Berlin and Prague, as well as her status in European high society. Bertha tried to sustain her relationship with Hayes after her divorce and his return to the United States, but declined his offer to legally adopt and raise their daughter.<ref name="kolowrat" />

The Bogdanoff twins made many grandiose and unsubstantiated claims about their early lives and ancestry: they claimed to have received IQ scores above 190 as children,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Risen |first=Clay |date=2022-01-07 |title=Grichka and Igor Bogdanoff, Twins in an Uneasy Spotlight, Die at 72 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/01/07/world/europe/grichka-and-igor-bogdanoff-dead.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108001558/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/01/07/world/europe/grichka-and-igor-bogdanoff-dead.html |archive-date=2022-01-08 |access-date=2024-03-20 |website=New York Times}}</ref> and that their father was "the descendant of a prince, the right arm of Tsar Peter the Great"<ref name="kolowrat" /> with ancestral links to a noble [[Muslim]] [[Tatars|Tatar]] [[Mirza (noble)|Mirza]] from [[Penza]] that converted to [[Eastern Orthodox Church|Orthodox Christianity]] in exchange for a royal title from [[Feodor III of Russia|Tsar Feodor III]].<ref>Après consultation de tous les nobiliaires faisant autorité, aucun ne mentionne une quelconque famille de prince Bogdanoff : Patrick de Gmeline. « Dictionnaire de la noblesse russe ». Éditions Contrepoint, 1978, Almanach de Gotha 1918, Almanach de Gotha 1940, Almanach de Gotha, 2013.</ref><ref>Cependant, cela ne les prive pas théoriquement de la possibilité de confirmer à nouveau leur droit au titre de prince sur les voies de la grâce du chef de la maison impériale de [[Russia|Russie]] (selon plusieurs exemples connus) : les Bogdanoff sont de nouveau cités comme famille princière en 1906 dans des dictionnaires généalogiques russes. La reconnaissance par le chef de la maison souveraine royale de Georgie, [[Irakli Bagration of Mukhrani|Irakli Bagration-Mukhraneli]], des droits de Youra Bogdanoff au titre de prince serait considérée en elle-même comme une raison juridique suffisante à sa confirmation dans la dignité princière au sein de l'empire de Russie. Un tel document confirmerait en effet du point de vue juridique la dignité princière et fixerait la tradition généalogique familiale de cette famille. C'est pourquoi Igor et Grichka Bogdanoff, ainsi que les enfants légitimes d'Igor, s'octroient le droit d'user aujourd'hui des titres de princes et princesses Bogdanoff (voir [http://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/alt.talk.royalty/sOef_cYjnms Lettre du Dr Stanislaw W. Dumin, président de la Fédération Russe de Généalogie et de la Société d'Histoire et de Généalogie à Moscou, Secrétaire général de l'Académie Internationale de Généalogie, et du prince Vadime Lopoukhine, vice-président de l'Assemblée de la Noblesse Russe: ''Certificat quant aux droits de Youri Mikhailovitch Bogdanoff et de sa descendance à la dignité et au titre princier''. 25 décembre 2001] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20160317214716/https://groups.google.com/forum/%23!topic/rec.sport.rugby.union/3CRJPEyFCaA#!topic/alt.talk.royalty/sOef_cYjnms |date=17 March 2016 }}</ref>{{citation needed|date=September 2022}} Genealogist [[William Addams Reitwiesner]] found little evidence for this, noting that "Other than a statement by Dr. Stanislaus Dumin (included in a message posted by the twins on 7 January 2005 to the alt.talk.royalty [[Usenet]] newsgroup) there isn't much evidence to support this claim."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.wargs.com/noble/bogdanov.html|title=Ancestry of Igor and Grichka Bogdanov|website=wargs.com}}</ref>

They made similarly grandiose claims about how their parents met, claiming that Yuri was "a young artist (...) (who) followed 'a solid training as a painter as a free auditor at the [[Beaux-Arts de Paris|Beaux-Arts]]'", and that "a 'famous writer' (...) introduced Yuri to their grandmother." These claims were the subject of extensive research by journalist Maud Guillaumin for the novel ''Le mystère Bogdanoff'' (L'Archipel, 2019), who concluded that the claims were rife with "approximations and historical inaccuracies": in reality, Guillaumin found out that Yuri Bogdanoff, in his teenage years, had first travelled to Spain from the [[Soviet Union]] and found himself unable to return on account of being declared a spy and imprisoned. Contrary to the twins' claims, their father had instead begun "a life of wandering from farm to [[Pyrenees|Pyrenean]] farm" as a labourer after arriving in France before eventually finding employment at Bertha's castle residence in 1948, which is where he met Maya. In an interview with the twins' godmother, Monique David, it was further established by Guillaumin that the twins' mother was already pregnant at the time of her marriage to Yuri, and that Bertha considered them an unworthy match. She "chased him away", leading to their subsequent divorce and his absence from the twins' lives until they were ten years old.<ref name="kolowrat" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.closermag.fr/people/igor-et-grischka-bogdanoff-le-triste-destin-de-leur-pere-youra-936785|title=Igor et Grischka Bogdanoff : le triste destin de leur pèr... - Closer|date=24 February 2019|website=closermag.fr}}</ref>

== Television shows ==
[[File:PHOTOS IGOR GRICHKA.jpg|thumb|Grichka (left) and Igor in the 1990s]]

The brothers began careers in television, hosting several popular programs on science and science fiction.<ref name="overbye">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/11/09/arts/are-they-geniuses-b-jokers-french-physicists-cosmic-theory-creates-big-bang-its.html?pagewanted=all |title=Are They a) Geniuses or b) Jokers?; French Physicists' Cosmic Theory Creates a Big Bang of Its Own |first=Dennis |last=Overbye |author-link=Dennis Overbye |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=9 November 2002 |page=B2}}</ref><ref name="chronicle"/><ref name="johnson">{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=George |author-link=George Johnson (writer) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/11/17/weekinreview/ideas-trends-in-theory-it-s-true-or-not.html?pagewanted=all |title=Ideas & Trends: In Theory, It's True (Or Not) |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=17 November 2002 |page=4004004}}</ref> The first of these, ''Temps X'' (''Time X''), ran from 1979 to 1989<ref name="chronicle">{{cite web |url=http://chronicle.com/article/The-Emperor-s-New-Science/11130 |title=The Emperor's New Science: French TV Stars Rock the World of Theoretical Physics |author=Richard Monastersky |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |date=5 November 2002 |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.spektrum.de/rezension/reise-zur-stunde-null/957293 |title=Eine Nullnummer |website=Spektrum.de |first=Frank |last=Schubert |date=14 June 2008 |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> and introduced several British and American science-fiction series to the French public, including ''[[Star Trek]]'', and ''[[Doctor Who]]'', in addition to featuring musical guests such as [[Jean-Michel Jarre]].<ref name="BBC22" />

In 2002, the Bogdanoffs launched a new weekly television show, ''Rayons X'', on the French public channel [[France 2]]. In August 2004, they presented a 90-minute special cosmology program.<ref name="fosse">{{cite news |last=Fossé |first=David |title=''La mystification Bogdanov'' |work=Ciel et Espace |pages=52–55 |date=October 2004 |url=http://ybmessager.free.fr/docs/ciel-et-espace-bogda1.pdf |access-date=21 July 2019 |language=fr |archive-date=23 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923113934/http://ybmessager.free.fr/docs/ciel-et-espace-bogda1.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Academic careers ==
Grichka Bogdanoff received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in mathematics from the [[University of Burgundy]] ([[Dijon]]) in 1999.<ref name="overbye"/><ref name="PHD">{{cite thesis |author=Grichka Bogdanoff |title=Fluctuations quantiques de la signature de la métrique à l'échelle de Planck |year=1999 |type=doctorate in mathematics |publisher=[[University of Burgundy]] |others=Supervised by Daniel Sternheimer |url=http://www.sudoc.abes.fr/xslt/DB=2.1/SET=5/TTL=1/CMD?ACT=SRCHM&ACT0=SRCH&MATCFILTER=Y&MATCSET=Y&NOSCAN=Y&PARSE_MNEMONICS=N&PARSE_OPWORDS=N&PARSE_OLDSETS=N&IMPLAND=Y&screen_mode=search&IKT0=1004&TRM0=bogdanoff+grichka&ACT1=*&IKT1=4&TRM1=fluctuations&ACT2=*&IKT2=1016&TRM2=&ACT3=*&IKT3=1016&TRM3=&SRT=RLV&ADI_TAA=&ADI_LND=&ADI_JVU=&ADI_MAT=B&ADI_MAT=T&ADI_MAT=F&ADI_MAT=O&ADI_MAT=A&ADI_MAT=M&ADI_MAT=N&ADI_MAT=G&ADI_MAT=V&ADI_MAT=I&ADI_MAT=K&ADI_MAT=Y&ADI_MAT=X&ILN_DEP_BIB=DEP&ADI_BIB= |format=entry in the French academic library directory}}</ref> In 2002, Igor Bogdanoff received a Ph.D. in theoretical physics from the University of Burgundy.<ref name="overbye" /> Both brothers received the lowest passing grade of "honorable" rather than the more usual "très honorable".<ref name="overbye"/>

===Bogdanov affair===
{{Main|Bogdanov affair}}

[[File:Igor and Grichka Bogdanoff.jpg|thumb|Igor (left) and Grichka Bogdanoff in 2010]]

In 2001 and 2002, the brothers published five papers (including "Topological field theory of the initial singularity of spacetime") in peer-reviewed physics journals.<ref name="bogdanov-spires">{{cite web |url=http://inspirehep.net/search?p=FIND+a+BOGDANOFF |title=INSPIRE-HEP citation information for Bogdanov papers |access-date=24 February 2018 |website=[[INSPIRE-HEP]]}}</ref><ref name='economist'>{{cite news |title=Publish and perish |url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2002/11/14/publish-and-perish |date=14 November 2002 |newspaper=The Economist}}</ref> Controversy over the Bogdanoffs' work began on 22 October 2002, with an email sent by [[University of Tours]] physicist Max Niedermaier to [[University of Pittsburgh]] physicist [[Ezra T. Newman]].<ref name="nature" /> Niedermaier suggested that the Bogdanoffs' Ph.D. theses and papers were "spoof[s]", created by throwing together instances of theoretical-physics jargon, including terminology from [[string theory]]: "The abstracts are delightfully meaningless combinations of buzzwords&nbsp;... which apparently have been taken seriously."<ref name="nature" /><ref name='newscientist'>{{cite news |first=Hazel |last=Muir |title=Twins raise ruckus |date=16 November 2002 |work=[[New Scientist]] |pages=6 |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg17623690-500-twins-raise-ruckus/ |access-date=11 July 2019 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Copies of the email reached American [[mathematical physicist]] [[John C. Baez]], and on 23 October he created a discussion thread about the Bogdanoffs' work on the Usenet newsgroup ''sci.physics.research'', titled "Physics bitten by reverse Alan Sokal hoax?"<ref name="chronicle" /><ref name="usenet">{{cite newsgroup |author=John Baez |title=Physics bitten by reverse Alan Sokal hoax? |date=24 October 2002 |newsgroup=sci.physics.research |message-id=ap7tq6$eme$1@glue.ucr.edu |url=https://groups.google.com/group/sci.physics.research/browse_frm/thread/28e04d38aabd16f2/09f8fde48d7c3566#09f8fde48d7c3566 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120805123439/http://groups.google.com/group/sci.physics.research/browse_frm/thread/28e04d38aabd16f2/09f8fde48d7c3566#09f8fde48d7c3566 |archive-date=2012-08-05}}</ref> Baez was comparing the Bogdanoffs' publications to the 1996 [[Sokal affair]], in which physicist [[Alan Sokal]] successfully submitted an intentionally nonsensical paper to a [[cultural studies]] journal in order to criticize that field's lax standards for discussing science. The Bogdanoffs quickly became a popular discussion topic, with most respondents agreeing that the papers were flawed.<ref name="economist" />

The story spread in public media, prompting Niedermaier to apologize to the Bogdanoffs, admitting that he had not read the papers himself. The Bogdanoffs' background in entertainment lent some plausibility to the idea that they were attempting a deliberate hoax, but Igor Bogdanoff quickly denied the accusation.<ref name="overbye" /><ref name="economist" />

In October 2002, the Bogdanoffs released an email containing apparently supportive statements by [[Laurent Freidel]], then a visiting professor at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]].<ref name="chronicle"/> Soon after, Freidel denied writing any such remarks, telling the press that he had forwarded a message containing that text to a friend.<ref name="chronicle"/>

The online discussion was quickly followed by media attention. ''[[The Register]]'' reported on the dispute on 1 November 2002,<ref name=register>{{cite web |last=Orlowski |first=Andrew |title=Physics hoaxers discover Quantum Bogosity |url=https://www.theregister.co.uk/2002/11/01/physics_hoaxers_discover_quantum_bogosity/ |website=[[The Register]] |author-link=Andrew Orlowski |date=1 November 2002 |access-date=27 February 2018}}</ref> and stories in ''[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]'',<ref name="chronicle" /> ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'',<ref name="nature" /> ''The New York Times'',<ref name="overbye" /> and other publications appeared soon after.<ref name="le-monde">{{cite web |language=fr |author=Hervé Morin |url=http://www-cosmosaf.iap.fr/Le%20Monde_fr%20%20La%20r%C3%A9putation%20scientifique%20contest%C3%A9e%20des%20fr%C3%A8res.htm |title=La réputation scientifique contestée des frères Bogdanov |work=[[Le Monde]] |date=19 December 2002 |access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="die-zeit"/> These news stories included commentary by physicists.

One of the scientists who approved Igor Bogdanoff's thesis, [[Roman Jackiw]] of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], spoke to ''[[The New York Times]]'' reporter [[Dennis Overbye]]. Overbye wrote that Jackiw was intrigued by the thesis, although it contained many points he did not understand. Jackiw defended the thesis.<ref name="overbye"/> In contrast, Ignatios Antoniadis (of the [[École Polytechnique]]), who approved Grichka Bogdanoff's thesis, later reversed his judgment of it. Antoniadis told ''[[Le Monde]]'':

<blockquote>I had given a favorable opinion for Grichka's defense, based on a rapid and indulgent reading of the thesis text. Alas, I was completely mistaken. The scientific language was just an appearance behind which hid incompetence and ignorance of even basic physics.<ref name="le-monde"/></blockquote>

The journal ''[[Classical and Quantum Gravity]]'' (CQG) published one of the Bogdanoffs' papers, titled "Topological field theory of the initial singularity of spacetime";<ref name="Bala">{{Cite book |author=Arun Bala |year=2016 |title=Complementarity Beyond Physics: Niels Bohr's Parallels |publisher=Palgrave MacMillan |pages=26–27}}</ref> Ian Russell, assistant director of its journals division, later issued a statement that "we deployed our standard peer-review process on that paper."<ref name="chronicle" /> After the article's publication and the publicity surrounding the controversy, mathematician [[Greg Kuperberg]] posted to Usenet a statement written by the journal's senior publisher, Andrew Wray, and its co-editor, Hermann Nicolai. The statement read, in part:

<blockquote>Regrettably, despite the best efforts, the refereeing process cannot be 100% effective. Thus the paper ... made it through the review process even though, in retrospect, it does not meet the standards expected of articles in this journal... The paper was discussed extensively at the annual Editorial Board meeting ... and there was general agreement that it should not have been published. Since then several steps have been taken to further improve the peer review process in order to improve the quality assessment on articles submitted to the journal and reduce the likelihood that this could happen again.<ref>{{cite newsgroup |title=If not a hoax, it's still an embarrassment |last=Kuperberg |first=Greg |author-link=Greg Kuperberg |date=2002-11-01 |newsgroup=sci.physics.research |message-id=apu93q$2a2$1@conifold.math.ucdavis.edu |url=https://groups.google.com/group/sci.physics.research/msg/c1437787f7e9909c |access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref></blockquote>

The statement was quoted in ''The New York Times,''<ref name="overbye"/> ''The Chronicle of Higher Education'',<ref name="chronicle"/> and ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]].''<ref name="nature">{{cite journal |last=Butler|first= Declan |title=Theses spark twin dilemma for physicists |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=420 |issue=5 |year=2002 |doi=10.1038/420005a |pages=5 |pmid=12422173 |bibcode=2002Natur.420Q...5B |doi-access=free}}</ref> Moreover, {{Lang|de|[[Die Zeit]]}} quoted Nicolai as saying that had the paper reached his desk, he would have immediately rejected it.<ref name="die-zeit">{{in lang|de}} Christoph Drösser, Ulrich Schnabel. "''[http://www.zeit.de/2002/46/Die_Maerchen_der_Gebrueder_Bogdanov Die Märchen der Gebrüder Bogdanov]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}''" ("Fairy tales of the Brothers Bogdanov") {{Lang|de|[[Die Zeit]]}} (2002), issue 46.</ref>

The ''[[Chinese Journal of Physics]]'' published Igor Bogdanoff's "The [[KMS state]] of spacetime at the [[Planck units#Planck scale|Planck scale]]", while ''[[Nuovo Cimento]]'' published "KMS space-time at the Planck scale". According to physicist Arun Bala, these papers "involved purported applications of quantum theory to understand processes at the dawn of the universe" but turned out to be a "hoax perpetrated on the physics community."<ref name="Bala" />

Eli Hawkins, acting as a referee on behalf of the ''[[Journal of Physics A]]'', suggested rejecting one of the Bogdanoffs' papers: "It would take up too much space to enumerate all the mistakes: indeed it is difficult to say where one error ends and the next begins."<ref name="telegraph">{{Cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2022/01/04/igor-grichka-bogdanoff-eccentric-french-tv-star-twins-centre/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2022/01/04/igor-grichka-bogdanoff-eccentric-french-tv-star-twins-centre/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Igor and Grichka Bogdanoff, eccentric French TV star twins at the centre of a notorious scientific controversy – obituary |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=4 January 2022 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Eventually, the controversy attracted mainstream media attention, opening new avenues for physicists' comments to be disseminated. ''[[Le Monde]]'' quoted [[Alain Connes]], recipient of the 1982 [[Fields Medal]], as saying, "I didn't need long to convince myself that they're talking about things that they haven't mastered."<ref name="le-monde"/> ''The New York Times'' reported that the physicists [[David Gross]], [[Carlo Rovelli]], and [[Lee Smolin]] considered the Bogdanoff papers nonsensical.<ref name="overbye"/> [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel laureate]] [[Georges Charpak]] later said on a French talk show that the Bogdanoffs' presence in the scientific community was "nonexistent".<ref>[[France 2]] TV talk show, ''Tout le monde en parle'', 12 June 2004. See {{cite web |url=https://www.nouvelobs.com/rue89/rue89-nos-vies-connectees/20100930.RUE8748/quand-charpak-parlait-de-son-nobel-et-faisait-le-mariole.html |title=Quand Charpak parlait de son Nobel (et faisait le mariole) |last=Riché |first=Pascal |website=[[L'Obs]] |date=30 September 2010 |access-date=21 November 2018 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name="acrimed">{{cite web |url=https://www.acrimed.org/Les-freres-Bogdanov-la-science-et-les-medias |title=Les frères Bogdanov, la science et les médias |website=Acrimed |date=29 November 2004 |access-date=11 January 2021 |language=fr}}</ref>

Robert Oeckl's official [[MathSciNet]] review of "Topological field theory of the initial singularity of spacetime" says that the paper is "rife with nonsensical or meaningless statements and suffers from a serious lack of coherence", gives several examples to illustrate his point, and concludes that the paper "falls short of scientific standards and appears to have no meaningful content."<ref name="oeckl">{{cite journal |last=Oeckl |first=Robert |title=Review of 'Topological field theory of the initial singularity of spacetime' |publisher=[[MathSciNet]] |mr=1894907}}</ref> An official report from the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS), which became public in 2010, concluded that the paper "''ne peut en aucune façon être qualifié de contribution scientifique''" ("cannot in any way be considered a scientific contribution").<ref name="huet2010">{{cite news |url=http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2010/10/15/un-document-accablant-pour-les-bogdanov/ |title=Un document accablant pour les Bogdanov |last=Huet |first=Sylvestre |work=[[Libération]] |date=15 October 2010 |access-date=21 July 2019 |language=fr |archive-date=12 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712152853/http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2010/10/15/un-document-accablant-pour-les-bogdanov/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://m0.libe.com/blogs/sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2010/10/15/rapp-bogdanovcopy.pdf |title=Rapport sur l'article "Topological field theory of the initial singularity of spacetime" |access-date=21 July 2019 |archive-date=21 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721174119/http://m0.libe.com/blogs/sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2010/10/15/rapp-bogdanovcopy.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The CNRS report summarized the Bogdanoffs' theses thus: "''Ces thèses n’ont pas de valeur scientifique. […] Rarement aura-t-on vu un travail creux habillé avec une telle sophistication''" ("These theses have no scientific value. [...] Rarely have we seen a hollow work dressed with such sophistication").<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |url=http://sciences.blog.lemonde.fr/2010/10/16/les-jumeaux-bogdanov-etrilles-par-le-cnrs/ |title=Les jumeaux Bogdanov étrillés par le CNRS |last=Parienté |first=Jonathan |date=16 October 2010 |work=En quête de sciences |access-date=24 February 2018 |publisher=[[Le Monde]] |language=fr-FR |archive-date=20 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110420002224/http://sciences.blog.lemonde.fr/2010/10/16/les-jumeaux-bogdanov-etrilles-par-le-cnrs/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="lexpress2015">{{cite news |url=https://lexpansion.lexpress.fr/actualite-economique/les-bogdanov-reclamaient-1-million-ils-sont-condamnes-a-payer-2000-euros_1695746.html |title=Les Bogdanov réclamaient un million, ils sont condamnés à payer 2000 euros |work=[[L'Express]] |date=2 July 2015 |access-date=25 February 2018 |language=fr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612162150/https://lexpansion.lexpress.fr/actualite-economique/les-bogdanov-reclamaient-1-million-ils-sont-condamnes-a-payer-2000-euros_1695746.html |archive-date=2018-06-12 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Lawsuits===
On 30 December 2004, the Bogdanoffs sued [[:fr:Ciel et Espace|''Ciel et Espace'']] for [[defamation]] over the publication of a critical article titled "The Mystification of the Bogdanoffs".<ref name="ciel-et-espace-judgment" /> In September 2006, the case was dismissed after the Bogdanoffs missed court deadlines; they were ordered to pay [[Euro|€]]2,500 to the magazine's publisher to cover its legal costs.<ref name="ciel-et-espace-judgment">{{cite news |title=''Les frères Bogdanov condamnés'' |work=Ciel et Espace |date=October 2006 |url=http://www.cieletespace.fr/Actualites/488_les,freres,bogdanov,condamnes.aspx |access-date=7 October 2006 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061117165918/http://www.cieletespace.fr/Actualites/488_les%2Cfreres%2Cbogdanov%2Ccondamnes.aspx |archive-date=17 November 2006}}</ref><ref name="obs">{{cite web |url=https://www.nouvelobs.com/medias/20061014.OBS0182/fin-du-litige-avec-ciel-et-espace.html |title=Fin du litige avec ''Ciel et Espace'' |website=[[L'Obs]] |date=14 October 2006 |access-date=25 February 2018 |language=fr}}</ref> There was never a substantive ruling on whether the Bogdanoffs had been defamed.<ref name="obs" />

{{anchor|Criminal prosecution of Alain Riazuelo}}Alain Riazuelo, an [[Astrophysics|astrophysicist]] at the [[Institut d'Astrophysique de Paris]], participated in many of the online discussions of the Bogdanoffs' work. He posted an unpublished version of Grichka Bogdanoff's Ph.D. thesis on his personal website, along with his critical analysis. Bogdanoff subsequently described this version as "dating from 1991 and too unfinished to be made public". Rather than suing Riazuelo for [[defamation]], Bogdanoff filed a criminal complaint of [[copyright]] (''droit d'auteur'') violation against him in May 2011.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2012/03/15/un-curieux-jugement-pour-les-jumeaux-bogdanov/ |title=Un curieux jugement pour les frères Bogdanov |last=Huet |first=Sylvestre |website=[[Libération]] |date=15 March 2012 |access-date=12 July 2019 |language=fr |archive-date=12 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712152828/http://sciences.blogs.liberation.fr/2012/03/15/un-curieux-jugement-pour-les-jumeaux-bogdanov/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The police detained and interrogated Riazuelo. He was convicted in March 2012. A fine of €2,000 the court imposed was suspended, and only €1.00 of damages was awarded,<ref name="auto"/> but in passing judgment the court said that the scientist had "lacked prudence", given "the fame of the plaintiff".<ref name=Foucart2012>{{cite news |last=Foucart |first=Stéphane |title=Les chercheurs et la menace Bogdanov (Researchers and the Bogdanov threat) |language=fr |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2012/04/20/les-chercheurs-et-la-menace-bogdanov_1688106_1650684.html |newspaper=[[Le Monde]] |date=20 April 2012}}</ref>

The verdict outraged many scientists, who felt that the police and courts should have no say in a discussion of the scientific merits of a piece of work. In April 2012, a group of 170 scientists published an open letter titled ''L'affaire Bogdanoff: Liberté, Science et Justice, Des scientifiques revendiquent leur droit au blâme'' (''The Bogdanoff Affair: Liberty, Science and Justice, scientists claim their right of critique'').<ref name=NouvObsApril2012>{{cite journal |title=Frères Bogdanov : 170 scientifiques réclament le droit de les critiquer |trans-title=Bogdanov brothers: 170 scientists claim the right of critique |url=http://rue89.nouvelobs.com/2012/04/26/freres-bogdanov-170-scientifiques-reclament-le-droit-de-les-critiquer-231613 |journal=[[L'Obs|Le Nouvel Observateur]] |language=fr |date=26 April 2012}}</ref>

In 2014, the Bogdanoffs sued the weekly magazine ''[[Marianne (magazine)|Marianne]]'' for defamation, on account of reporting the magazine had published in 2010<ref name="marianne">{{cite news |last=Gathié |first=Nathalie |work=[[Marianne (magazine)|Marianne]] |title=Le vrai visage des Bogdanoff |date=16 October 2010 |language=fr |volume=74 |page=62}}</ref> that had brought the CNRS report to light. The magazine was eventually ordered to pay €64,000 in damages, much less than the €800,000 each that the Bogdanoffs originally demanded.<ref name="lepoint2014">{{cite web |url=https://www.lepoint.fr/medias/les-freres-bogdanoff-font-condamner-marianne-20-05-2014-1826187_260.php |title=Les frères Bogdanov font condamner "Marianne" |website=[[Le Point]] |language=fr |date=21 May 2014 |access-date=21 July 2019}}</ref> The Bogdanoffs also sued the CNRS for €1.2 million in damages, claiming that the CNRS report had "''porté atteinte à leur honneur, à leur réputation et à leur crédit''" ("undermined their honor, reputation and credit") and calling the report committee a "''Stasi scientifique''", but a tribunal ruled against them in 2015 and ordered them to pay €2,000.<ref name="lexpress2015"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/societe/article/2018/06/27/igor-et-grichka-bogdanov-quarante-ans-d-affaires-et-de-succes-populaires_5321914_3224.html |title=Igor et Grichka Bogdanov, 40 ans d'affaires et de succès populaires |last=Auffret |first=Simon |language=fr |work=[[Le Monde]] |date=27 June 2018 |access-date=22 July 2019}}</ref>

===Megatrend University===
In 2005, the Bogdanoffs became professors at [[Megatrend University]], a [[diploma mill]] from [[Belgrade]], where they were appointed to Chairs of [[Cosmology]] and made directors of the 'Megatrend Laboratory of Cosmology'.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.megatrend.edu.rs/profesori.php?bs%3Dgrichka_bogdanoff%26language%3D1 |title=Prof. Grichka Bogdanoff, PhD & Prof. Igor Bogdanoff, PhD |access-date=27 February 2018 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714205449/http://www.megatrend.edu.rs/profesori.php?bs=grichka_bogdanoff&language=1 |archive-date=14 July 2014 |website=[[Megatrend University]]}}</ref><ref name="politika">{{cite web |url=http://www.politika.rs/scc/clanak/295992/Kako-je-Mica-rektor-postao-kosmolog |script-title=sr:Како је Мића ректор постао космолог |first=Ана |last=Оташевић |website=politika.rs |date=10 June 2014 |access-date=27 February 2018 |language=sr}}</ref> [[Mića Jovanović]], the [[rector (academia)|rector]] and owner of Megatrend University, wrote a preface for the [[Serbian language|Serbian]] edition of ''Avant le Big Bang.''<ref name="politika"/> Jovanović himself later became embroiled in controversy and resigned his post when he was found out to not have obtained a Ph.D. at the [[London School of Economics]], as he had claimed.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-serbia-education-fraud/the-minister-his-mentor-and-the-fight-against-a-suspect-system-in-serbia-idUKKBN0EY1EV20140623 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124124556/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-serbia-education-fraud/the-minister-his-mentor-and-the-fight-against-a-suspect-system-in-serbia-idUKKBN0EY1EV20140623 |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 November 2017 |title=The minister, his mentor and the fight against a suspect system in Serbia |last=Robinson |first=Matt |date=23 June 2014 |access-date=27 February 2018 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> This scandal, combined with the presence of the Bogdanoffs, contributed to an atmosphere of controversy surrounding Megatrend.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/bogus-academic-claims-tarnish-serbias-ivory-tower-035622394.html |title=Bogus academic claims tarnish Serbia's ivory tower |website=[[Yahoo! News]] |publisher=[[Agence France-Presse]] |date=26 June 2014 |access-date=27 February 2018 |last=Subasic |first=Katarina |archive-date=28 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228041819/https://www.yahoo.com/news/bogus-academic-claims-tarnish-serbias-ivory-tower-035622394.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Personal lives and deaths ==
The Bogdanoff twins, who denied having undergone [[plastic surgery]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-01-04 |title=France's Bogdanoff TV twins die of Covid six days apart |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59867046 |access-date=2022-03-27}}</ref> became known for their extremely prominent cheekbones and elongated chins. In 2010, ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'' described the twins' [[cheekbones]] as "so high and bulbous as to appear to threaten their owners' vision", adding that the twins' appearance at the [[Cannes Film Festival]] had "caused a stir around the world". The ''Herald'' noted that the twins' cheekbones had become noticeably larger in the 1990s, and that "growth in their lips and chins continued unabated through the last decade".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/celebrity/who-are-those-jawdropping-twins-20100521-w08l.html |title=Who are those jaw-dropping twins? |last=Robinson |first=Georgina |date=21 May 2012 |access-date=18 September 2021 |work=Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> According to former [[Ministry of National Education (France)|education minister]] [[Luc Ferry]], a friend of the brothers, they had both received [[Botulinum toxin#Cosmetic uses|botox injections for cosmetic treatment]].<ref name="BBC22">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-59867046 |title=France's Bogdanoff TV twins die of Covid six days apart |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=4 January 2022 |website=[[bbc.co.uk]] |access-date=4 January 2022}}</ref>

The twins became popular [[Internet meme]]s, especially among enthusiasts of [[cryptocurrency]], jokingly depicting the Bogdanoffs as "all-powerful market makers". Their status as "crypto memes" was covered by several outlets upon their deaths, including [[CNN]], ''[[Business Insider]]'', and ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''.<ref name="telegraph" /><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/04/entertainment/igor-bogdanoff-dies-covid-intl-scli/index.html |title=French TV star Igor Bogdanoff dies of Covid, days after twin brother |last1=Mawad |first1=Dalal |last2=Ataman |first2=Joseph |work=CNN |date=4 January 2022 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref><ref name="insider">{{Cite web |url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/bogdanoff-twins-death-covid-wall-street-bets-crypto-meme-2022-1 |title=Wall Street Bets mourns loss of crypto-meme-famous Bogdanoff twins, who died of COVID-19 |last=Dailey |first=Natasha |work=Business Insider |date=4 January 2022 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref> The twins "went along with their meme fame", according to ''Business Insider'', and said they predicted cryptocurrency in the 1980s on ''Temps X''.<ref name="insider" />

Besides French, they spoke German, Russian, and English.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2021/12/29/bogdanoff-twins-before-surgery/ |title=Bogdanoff twins before surgery look explored as Grichka and Igor die at 72 |last=Mustafa |first=Filiz |work=HITC |date=29 December 2021 |accessdate=4 January 2022 |archive-date=4 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220104211835/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2021/12/29/bogdanoff-twins-before-surgery/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Igor Bogdanoff had six children, four from his first marriage and two from his second.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Média |first=Prisma |title=Igor Bogdanov, six fois papa |url=https://www.gala.fr/l_actu/news_de_stars/igor_bogdanov_six_fois_papa_335587 |access-date=2022-01-01 |website=Gala.fr |date=12 February 2015 |language=fr}}</ref> He married his second wife, Princess Amélie of [[Bourbon-Parma]], daughter of [[Prince Michel of Bourbon-Parma]], civilly in Paris on 1 October 2009 and religiously in [[Château de Chambord|Chambord]] two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Igor convole à Chambord |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2009/09/30/683852-igor-convole-a-chambord.html |access-date=2022-01-01 |website=ladepeche.fr |language=fr}}</ref> Grichka was in a relationship with a woman named Chaymae at the time of his death, but never married and had no children.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bellecour |first1=Mathilde |title=Mort des frères Bogdanoff : qui est la compagne de Grichka qui a appelé les pompiers lorsqu'il est tombé malade ? |url=https://www.voici.fr/news-people/mort-des-freres-bogdanoff-qui-est-la-compagne-de-grichka-qui-a-appele-les-pompiers-720413 |website=[[Voici]] |access-date=27 April 2023 |language=French |date=6 January 2022}}</ref> The twins declared having been diagnosed with [[Asperger syndrome]],<ref>{{cite web |last1=Grunwald |first1=Déborah |title=Dans le rétro : Igor et Grichka Bogdanoff |url=https://www.francebleu.fr/emissions/dans-le-retro/dans-le-retro-igor-et-grichka-bogdanoff |website=[[France Bleu]] |access-date=27 April 2023 |language=French |date=6 December 2021}}</ref> but that has not been confirmed.

===Deaths===
The Bogdanoff twins were both hospitalized, at the [[Hôpital Européen Georges-Pompidou|Georges Pompidou European Hospital]] in Paris,<ref name="auto1" /> in [[Medical state|critical condition]] on 15 December 2021, after contracting [[COVID-19]]. Grichka died on 28 December,<ref name="auto2">{{cite news |title=Grichka Bogdanoff, l'un des jumeaux stars des années 1980, est mort du Covid-19 |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/disparitions/article/2021/12/28/grichka-l-un-des-deux-freres-bogdanoff-est-mort_6107525_3382.html |access-date=28 December 2021 |publisher=Le Monde |date=28 December 2021}}</ref> and Igor on 3 January 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Igor Bogdanoff est mort, six jours après son frère jumeau Grichka |url=https://www.nouvelobs.com/coronavirus-de-wuhan/20220103.OBS52819/igor-bogdanoff-est-mort-six-jours-apres-son-frere-jumeau-grichka.html |access-date=3 January 2022 |work=[[L'Obs]] |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |date=3 January 2022 |language=fr}}</ref> They were 72 and both [[Vaccine hesitancy|intentionally unvaccinated]].<ref name="auto2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mort d'Igor Bogdanoff, six jours après son frère Grichka |url=https://www.bfmtv.com/people/mort-d-igor-bogdanoff-six-jours-apres-son-frere-grichka_AN-202201030363.html |access-date=2022-01-04 |website=BFMTV |date=3 January 2022 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name="BBC22" /> The funeral for both twins was held on 10 January 2022, in the [[La Madeleine, Paris|Church of the Madeleine]], in [[Paris]], France.<ref name="ouest_france">{{cite news |language=fr |title=Les obsèques des frères Bogdanoff célébrées dans l'intimité de l'église de la Madeleine à Paris |work=Ouest France |date=10 January 2022 |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sante/virus/coronavirus/les-obseques-des-freres-bogdanoff-celebrees-dans-l-intimite-de-l-eglise-de-la-madeleine-a-paris-64120a54-722f-11ec-9387-6c239fe68028 |access-date=16 January 2022}}.</ref>

== Publications ==
The Bogdanoff brothers published a number of works in science fiction, philosophy and [[popular science]]. Since 1991, they signed their books as "Bogdanov", preferring "v" to "ff".
* ''Clefs pour la science-fiction'' (essay), Éditions Seghers, 378 p., Paris, 1976 {{ISBN missing}}, BNF:34707099q.
* ''L'Effet science-fiction: à la recherche d'une définition'' (essay), Éditions Robert Laffont, Paris, 1979, 423 p., {{ISBN|978-2-221-00411-1}}, BNF:34650185&nbsp;g.
* ''Chroniques du "Temps X"'' (preface by Gérard Klein), Éditions du Guépard, Paris, 1981, 247 p., {{ISBN|978-2-86527-030-9}}, BNF: 34734883f.
* ''La Machine fantôme'', Éditions J'ai lu, 1985, 251 p., {{ISBN|978-2-277-21921-7}}, BNF:34842073t.
* ''La Mémoire double'' (novel), first as hardcover on Éditions Hachette, Paris, 1985, 381 p., {{ISBN|978-2-01-011494-6}}, BNF:348362498; then as pocket book
* ''Dieu et la science: vers le métaréalisme'' (interviews with Jean Guitton): Hardcover Éditions Grasset, Paris, 1991, 195 p., {{ISBN|978-2-246-42411-6}}, BNF: 35458968t; then as a pocketbook
* ''Avant le Big Bang: la création du monde'' (essay), 2004<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.slate.fr/story/54131/freres-bogdanoff |title=Les frères Bogdanoff: mentalistes de la science (fiction) |language=fr |work=Slate.fr |last=Alberganti |first=Michel |date=27 April 2012 |accessdate=4 January 2022}}</ref>
* ''Voyage vers l'Instant Zéro'', Éditions EPA, Paris, 2006, 185 p., {{ISBN|978-2-85120-635-0}}, BNF: 40986028h.
* ''Nous ne sommes pas seuls dans l'univers'', Éditions EPA, Paris, 2007, 191 p., {{ISBN|978-2-85120-664-0}}, BNF: 411885989.
* ''Au commencement du temps'', Éditions Flammarion, Paris, 2009, 317 p., {{ISBN|978-2-08-120832-2}}, BNF: 420019981.
* ''Le Visage de Dieu'', (with a preface by Robert Woodrow Wilson and endnotes by Jim Peebles, Robert Woodrow Wilson and John Mather, Éditions Grasset, Paris, May 2010, 282 p., {{ISBN|978-2-246-77231-6}}, BNF: 42207600f.
* ''Le Dernier Jour des dinosaures'' Éditions de la Martinière, Octobre 2011, {{ISBN|978-2732447100}}
* ''La Pensée de Dieu'', (with endnotes by Luis Gonzalez-Mestres), Éditions Grasset, Paris, June 2012, {{ISBN|978-2-246-78509-5}}
* ''Le mystère du satellite Planck'' ''(Qu'y avait-il avant le Big Bang ?)'' (with preface and endnotes by Luis Gonzalez-Mestres, Éditions Eyrolles, June 2013, {{ISBN|978-2-212-55732-9}}
* ''La Fin du hasard'', Éditions Grasset, Paris, Octobre 2013, {{ISBN|978-2-246-80990-6}}
* ''3 minutes pour comprendre la grande théorie du Big Bang'' (preface by John Mather, end notes by Luis Gonzalez-Mestres, Éditions Le Courrier du Livre, October 2014, {{ISBN|978-2702911211}}
